sourceChanges.citationTitle: Microsoft Copilot and general guidelines for using generative AI tools
Microsoft Copilot and general guidelines for using generative AI tools | IT Services - McGill University
Principles on Generative AI in Teaching and Learning at McGill
Using generative AI in teaching and learning

claimChanges.claimText: Microsoft Copilot Commercial Data Protection is listed for McGill University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.

McGill recommends that instructors explain to students in their course outline what the appropriate use or non-use is of generative AI tools in the context of that course. The use or non-use of these tools should align with the learning outcomes associated with the course.

McGill explicitly rejects DeepSeek AI for McGill-managed or research-funded devices, rejects Read.AI and other AI meeting bots for McGill use, and says tools not mentioned in the available AI tools list are automatically considered rejected.

McGill's Provost-endorsed principles state that instructors remain responsible for comporting themselves according to the highest standards of academic integrity in their use of generative AI tools. Instructors must be explicit in course outlines about the expectations for use of generative AI tools and may set limits on their use in assessment tasks.
McGill lists Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat as an available AI tool for staff, faculty, and students, and says a secure version with enterprise data protection is available for all McGill users.

McGill guidance says users should mitigate potential privacy concerns by removing personally identifying information when using AI tools, be careful with sensitive or restricted material, and avoid using Personal Health Information (PHI) or Payment Card Industry (PCI) data with AI tools.

claimChanges.claimText: Read.AI is listed for McGill University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: restricted or blocked. Derived endorsement type: third party service.
DeepSeek AI is listed for McGill University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: restricted or blocked. Derived endorsement type: third party service.

Microsoft Teams Premium with AI Features is listed for McGill University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.
Microsoft Copilot Studio is listed for McGill University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.
ChatGPT Edu (OpenAI) is listed for McGill University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.
Synthesia is listed for McGill University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: institutionally licensed or procured.
Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is listed for McGill University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: institutionally licensed or procured.

McGill recommends that instructors explain to students in their course outline what the appropriate use or non-use is of generative AI tools in the context of that course. The use or non-use of these tools should align with the learning outcomes associated with the course.

McGill explicitly rejects DeepSeek AI for McGill-managed or research-funded devices, rejects Read.AI and other AI meeting bots for McGill use, and says tools not mentioned in the available AI tools list are automatically considered rejected.

McGill's Provost-endorsed principles state that instructors remain responsible for comporting themselves according to the highest standards of academic integrity in their use of generative AI tools. Instructors must be explicit in course outlines about the expectations for use of generative AI tools and may set limits on their use in assessment tasks.
McGill lists Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat as an available AI tool for staff, faculty, and students, and says a secure version with enterprise data protection is available for all McGill users.

McGill guidance says users should mitigate potential privacy concerns by removing personally identifying information when using AI tools, be careful with sensitive or restricted material, and avoid using Personal Health Information (PHI) or Payment Card Industry (PCI) data with AI tools.
